q: what is the fastest bird in the world
a: The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird in the world. In its hunting dive (stoop), it can reach speeds over 320 km/h (200 mph), making it the fastest animal on Earth in flight. In level flight, the fastest bird is the common swift, which can reach about 110 km/h (69 mph). Peregrine falcons are found on every continent except Antarctica, and their name comes from the Latin 'peregrinus', meaning wanderer. They hunt by diving at their prey — usually other birds — and striking it in mid-air.

The largest mammal in the world is the blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus), which is also the largest animal ever known to have lived. Adult blue whales can reach 30 meters (98 feet) long and weigh up to 200 tonnes — a newborn blue whale calf already weighs about 3 tonnes. The largest land mammal is the African bush elephant, which can weigh up to 6 tonnes. The largest non-cetacean marine mammal is the southern elephant seal. Blue whales feed almost exclusively on tiny krill, consuming up to 4 tonnes a day.

q: what is the most expensive painting
most expensive painting in the world
what is the most expensive painting ever sold
a: The most expensive painting ever sold is Leonardo da Vinci's 'Salvator Mundi' (Savior of the World), which sold at Christie's in November 2017 for $450.3 million — the highest price ever paid for a work of art at auction. The painting depicts Jesus Christ and was rediscovered in 2005 after centuries of neglect, with heavy overpainting. Its authenticity has been debated among scholars. Other record-breaking paintings include Willem de Kooning's 'Interchange' ($300 million, private sale) and Pablo Picasso's 'Les Femmes d'Alger' ($179.4 million at auction in 2015).

q: what is the longest bridge in the world
a: The longest bridge in the world is the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge in China, part of the Beijing–Shanghai high-speed railway. It is about 164.8 kilometers (102.4 miles) long and opened in 2011. It crosses the Yangtze River delta region, including a section over the Yangtze River itself. The longest bridge over water is the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge at about 55 kilometers (34 miles). The longest suspension bridge by main span is the Çanakkale 1915 Bridge in Turkey (2,023 meters), and the longest cable-stayed bridge is the Russky Bridge in Russia.

q: what is the largest empire in history
a: The largest empire in history by land area was the British Empire, which at its peak in 1920 controlled about 35.5 million square kilometers (13.7 million square miles) — roughly a quarter of the world's land area — and ruled about 23% of the world's population. The Mongol Empire was the largest contiguous land empire, covering about 24 million square kilometers (9.3 million square miles) in the 13th century. The Russian Empire (22.8 million km²) and the Qing Dynasty of China (14.7 million km²) were also among the largest. The British Empire was so large that it was said 'the sun never sets' on it.

q: who is the fastest man in the world
a: The fastest man in the world is Usain Bolt of Jamaica, who set the 100-meter world record of 9.58 seconds at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin — a top speed of about 44.7 km/h (27.8 mph). Bolt also holds the 200-meter record of 19.19 seconds, set at the same meet, and is the only sprinter to win the 100m, 200m, and 4x100m relay at three consecutive Olympics (2008, 2012, 2016). He was nicknamed 'Lightning Bolt'. The fastest woman is Florence Griffith-Joyner, whose 10.49-second 100m record from 1988 still stands.

q: what is the oldest living thing
what is the oldest living organism
a: The oldest known living organism is a Great Basin bristlecone pine (Pinus longaeva) in California's White Mountains, named Methuselah, which is about 4,850 years old. However, clonal organisms can be far older: the Pando aspen grove in Utah is a single genetic individual estimated at 80,000 years old, and a seagrass clone (Posidonia oceanica) in the Mediterranean is estimated at up to 100,000 years old. The oldest animal is a quahog clam nicknamed Ming, found off Iceland, which lived 507 years. The oldest tree species record belongs to 'Prometheus', also a bristlecone pine, cut down in 1964 at an estimated 4,900 years old.

q: what is the strongest animal relative to its size
a: It depends on how you measure strength. Relative to its body weight, the strongest animal is the dung beetle, which can pull 1,141 times its own body weight — the equivalent of a human pulling six double-decker buses. The leafcutter ant can carry about 50 times its body weight. In absolute terms, the African bush elephant is the strongest land animal, capable of lifting about 9,000 kg, and the blue whale is the strongest animal overall. The strongest bite belongs to the saltwater crocodile, with a bite force of about 3,700 psi.

The largest bird in the world is the ostrich, which stands up to 2.7 meters (9 feet) tall and can weigh up to 150 kg (330 pounds). Ostriches are flightless and native to Africa; they can run at up to 70 km/h (43 mph), making them the fastest running birds. The largest flying bird is the wandering albatross, with a wingspan of up to 3.5 meters (11.5 feet), followed by the great white pelican and the Dalmatian pelican. The tallest flying bird is the sarus crane. The largest bird ever was the extinct elephant bird of Madagascar, which stood up to 3 meters tall.

The largest reptile in the world is the saltwater crocodile (Crocodylus porosus), which can reach over 6 meters (20 feet) long and weigh over 1,000 kg (2,200 pounds). It is found in coastal waters and rivers from eastern India through Southeast Asia to northern Australia. The largest lizard is the Komodo dragon, up to 3 meters (10 feet) long, and the largest snake is the green anaconda, which can reach over 5 meters (16 feet) and weigh over 90 kg (200 pounds). The largest turtle is the leatherback sea turtle, which can weigh up to 900 kg.

The largest fish in the world is the whale shark (Rhincodon typus), which can reach over 12 meters (40 feet) long and weigh over 20 tonnes. Despite its size, the whale shark is a gentle filter feeder that eats plankton and small fish, and it is found in warm oceans worldwide. The largest bony fish is the ocean sunfish (Mola mola), which can weigh over 2 tonnes. The largest freshwater fish is the Mekong giant catfish or the beluga sturgeon, both of which can reach about 300 kg or more.

q: what is the largest land animal
largest land animal in the world
what is the biggest land animal
a: The largest land animal is the African bush elephant (Loxodonta africana), which can stand up to 4 meters (13 feet) tall at the shoulder and weigh up to 6 tonnes. African elephants are found in savannas and forests across sub-Saharan Africa, and they are highly intelligent, social animals that live in matriarchal herds. The largest land animal ever was the titanosaur Patagotitan, a sauropod dinosaur estimated at 37 meters (121 feet) long and weighing about 70 tonnes. The largest carnivorous land animal today is the polar bear, with males weighing up to 800 kg.
